$comment: Read from Google's own discovery document, not docs prose: spreadsheets.values.append -> POST v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}/values/{range}:append, request ValueRange, response AppendValuesResponse.
title: Google Sheets row
description: Append a row to a Google Sheet.
$idempotencyComment: Google offers no idempotency key on values.append -- there is no header and no parameter for one in the discovery document. So this is honestly unsafe-to-replay with no way to make it safe: a retried durable run appends a SECOND row. Saying so is better than implying a guarantee the API cannot give.

request.$pathComment: TWO config values in the URL, which no provider before Google needed. The `:append` suffix is part of the path, not a placeholder -- Google's custom-method syntax.

config.label: Spreadsheet ID
config.description: The long id from the sheet's URL: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/THIS_PART/edit.

config.label: Range
config.description: Where to append, in A1 notation. Google finds the last row of this range and writes below it.
config.$comment: A range contains `!` and can contain spaces, and a sheet named `Q1/Q2` contains a SLASH. Interpolated raw it changes which URL is called, and Google answers 404 about a spreadsheet rather than about encoding. Every emitter URL-encodes this, and a test asserts it in all three runtimes.

config.label: Row values
config.description: The cells of the row, comma separated. Left to right from the start of the range.

send.$comment: encoding `rows`, not `array`. Google's ValueRange.values is an array of ARRAYS -- the outer list is rows and the inner one is cells. A flat array is rejected as the wrong type, and a single row has to be wrapped: [[a, b, c]].

config.label: How to interpret the values
config.description: USER_ENTERED parses the cells the way typing them would -- so =SUM(A1:A2) becomes a formula and 1/2/26 becomes a date. RAW stores exactly the characters given.

options.label: As if typed (formulas and dates parsed)

config.$comment: In the QUERY of a POST, which the derived slot could not express. Sent in the body Google ignores it silently and defaults to RAW -- so an author who asked for formulas gets text that looks like a formula and never calculates. The discovery document lists a third enum value, INPUT_VALUE_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED, which is a protobuf artefact nobody would choose; it is deliberately not offered.

config.label: When the range already has data below
config.description: INSERT_ROWS pushes existing rows down. OVERWRITE writes into them.

outputShape.description: The spreadsheet that was written to.
The range Google actually wrote, in A1 notation. NOT the range that was asked for -- append finds the first empty row below it.
